sentences.text: Anna always felt overwhelmed.
She had big dreams but didn't know where to start.
She wanted to write a book, learn to play the guitar, and run a marathon.
But every time she thought about these goals, she felt stuck.
One day, Anna's friend, Lisa, gave her some advice.
"Why don't you try taking small steps?"
Lisa suggested.
"You don't have to do everything at once.
Just start with one small thing."
Anna decided to give it a try.
She started with her book.
Instead of writing a whole chapter, she wrote just one page each day.
At first, it seemed too little, but soon, she had written ten pages.
Then twenty.
Slowly, her book began to take shape.
Next, Anna picked up the guitar.
She practiced for just ten minutes each day.
It wasn't much, but it was something.
After a few weeks, she could play a simple song.
She felt proud of her progress.
Finally, Anna started training for the marathon.
She began by running for five minutes each morning.
It was hard at first, but she kept going.
Each week, she added a few more minutes to her run.
After a few months, she could run for an hour without stopping.
Anna realized that small steps made a big difference.
She didn't feel overwhelmed anymore.
Instead, she felt motivated and excited.
She saw progress in her book, her guitar playing, and her running.
One evening, Anna and Lisa met for coffee.
Anna shared her progress with Lisa.
"I can't believe how much I've done," Anna said.
"Your advice really worked."
Lisa smiled.
"I'm glad to hear that.
Remember, it's all about small steps.
They add up over time."
Anna nodded.
She knew she still had a long way to go, but she felt confident.
She had learned the power of small steps.
And with that, she knew she could achieve anything she set her mind to.
